reason: Radioactive heating should develop the interior of a rocky planetesimal, which is relevant to exposing stone and metal.
expectation: The rocky bodies will heat internally, potentially allowing their materials to separate.

effect: The rocky planetesimal has melted, making separation of its interior materials a plausible next step.
reaction: The qualification that not all asteroids melt is useful.
reason: Gravity should help dense metal sink within the melting body, separating it from the rock.
expectation: The body will develop distinct metal-rich and rocky layers.

effect: The melted body differentiated into a metal core and silicate material; collisions may now expose those layers.
reaction: The early differentiation of a small body is a useful detail.
reason: Collisions between small bodies should break open the differentiated world and expose its interior.

choice.combine: A small world with a metal core

expectation: The collision will expose fragments of stone and metal.

effect: The collision exposed metal core fragments, but the stone and water-related goals remain to be pursued.
reaction: The connection to iron meteorites is interesting.
reason: Radioactive heating could melt ice within an icy planetesimal, allowing water to interact with its rock.
expectation: The icy body will warm enough for some of its ice to melt.

effect: Internal heating produced liquid water inside the icy body, making water–rock interaction the next likely step.
reaction: The possibility of liquid water beneath a frozen exterior is interesting.
reason: Silicate grains provide rock for the liquid water to interact with, matching the altered-rock goal.

choice.combine: Liquid water inside an icy body

expectation: Water will react with the silicate rock, producing water-bearing altered minerals.

effect: Water reacted with silicates to make hydrated asteroid rock, completing the water goal. The stone-and-metal goal remains.
reaction: It's useful to see how hydrogen can remain bound in rock after exposed ice disappears.
reason: The core fragments exposed metal but did not complete the other goal; inspecting them may reveal how to obtain the needed stone as well.
expectation: The inspection will show available partners that might help complete the remaining goal.

effect: The core fragments have no available combinations, so the remaining stone must be exposed by another route.
reaction: That rules out combining the fragments further.
reason: Inspecting the collisions should reveal which remaining bodies they can break apart.
expectation: The report will identify a collision partner that can expose rocky material.

effect: Collisions have no currently available partners, so exposing stone requires another route.
reaction: That is surprising after the collision exposed the core.
reason: The differentiated small world may have another available operation that exposes its rocky material.

choice.inspect: A small world with a metal core

expectation: The inspection will identify any remaining partners for the differentiated body.

effect: The differentiated asteroid has cooled and solidified, making it a new candidate for a disruptive collision.
reaction: Cooling the rocky exterior first clarifies the missing step.
reason: A collision may now break the cooled asteroid and expose its rocky and metal-rich layers.
expectation: The collision will produce fragments exposing stone and metal.

effect: The collision exposed fragments of the asteroid’s rocky layers and completed the remaining goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the rocky fragments complement the earlier exposed core metal.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making water-bearing asteroid rock showed how hydrogen can remain in hydrated minerals even after exposed ice is gone.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the core fragments and collisions yielded no available partners, leaving the route to the remaining goal unclear.

surprise.text: The differentiated asteroid had to cool before another collision could expose its rocky layers; the earlier collision had already exposed core fragments.

arbitrary.text: Cooling before exposing rocky fragments made sense once explained, but it was not obvious why the earlier collision exposed only core material.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the links between asteroid interiors, meteorites and water-bearing minerals made me curious about how those materials contribute to Earth.
